data.description:
## Description

**What**: Implement the LiteLLM-backed provider abstraction in `dso_ci_review/providers/` for Anthropic and OpenAI, with exact-version pinning across LiteLLM and all transitive deps, a CI lint step that rejects loose pinning, and a stub mock provider that proves the abstraction is genuinely extensible (Gemini follow-on epic = config + new file only).

**Why**: SC2 of the epic. The provider abstraction is the replacement for `llm-api-call.sh`'s hand-rolled per-provider bash branches. Exact pinning across the dep tree closes the supply-chain attack class confirmed in March 2026 and prevents transitive bumps (especially `httpx`) from invalidating the S1 transport-verification artifact at runtime.

**Scope**:
- IN: `providers/` package with common interface + Anthropic + OpenAI clients via LiteLLM; integration tests exercising each provider end-to-end against fixture diffs; lockfile pinning LiteLLM AND all transitive deps at exact `==` versions; CI lint rejecting `~=`/`>=` operators across the entire lockfile; reproducible lockfile generation (uv lock or pip-compile with hashes); fail-loud config validation distinguishing missing-key (config error) from invalid-key (auth failure); 3rd-provider stub (mock) added as proof of extensibility.
- OUT: Full orchestration (S3); classifier and findings normalization (S3); parity test (S4); unit tests beyond what integration tests cover (S5); Gemini provider (separate placeholder epic).

## Done Definitions

- When this story is complete, the `providers/` package exposes Anthropic and OpenAI client implementations behind a common interface, both functional in CI runs and verified by an integration test exercising each provider end-to-end against fixture diffs.
  ← Satisfies: "LiteLLM-backed provider abstraction: Anthropic and OpenAI both functional in CI runs"
- When this story is complete, LiteLLM is pinned at an exact version (`litellm==<v>`) AND every transitive dependency in the lockfile is also pinned at an exact version. A CI lint step scans the lockfile and rejects any `~=` or `>=` operator on any line. Lockfile generation is reproducible (e.g., `uv lock` or `pip-compile` with hashes).
  ← Satisfies: "LiteLLM is pinned to an exact version ... compatible-release and range pinning are explicitly rejected by a CI lint step"
- When this story is complete, a stub `mock` provider implementation under `providers/` is added in tests as the third provider, proving extensibility — adding the Gemini follow-on epic requires only a new entry under `providers/` plus a config key, with no changes to `runner.py`, `dispatch.py`, or `findings.py`.
  ← Satisfies: "Adding the Gemini follow-on epic requires only a new entry under `providers/` plus a config key ... Verified by adding a stub `mock` provider in tests as the third implementation"
- When this story is complete, the runner refuses to run with a clear diagnostic when `providers/` config is missing or malformed, distinguishing missing-key (config error) from invalid-key (auth failure). It does not silently default to a provider that may not be authorized.
  ← Satisfies: "Provider routing must fail-loud on missing/malformed config" (Risk Register #8)

## Considerations

- [Reliability] Exact-version pinning is required across the entire lockfile, not just the LiteLLM line — transitive bumps (especially `httpx`) can swap the runtime transport and invalidate S1's transport-verification artifact (red-team finding).
- [Reliability/Security] Anthropic + OpenAI require distinct API keys; verify CI secrets configuration exposes both before integration tests run. Auth-failure error messages from SDKs sometimes contain partial credentials — ensure error entries written to the PR (per S3 partial-failure behavior) redact key values.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: As a maintainer, I have a LiteLLM-backed provider abstraction with exact-version pinning and proven extensibility
